newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News-Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News-Nov 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

At a six-and-a-half hour Coles Myer annual general meeting yesterday, which saw the company criticised by many of the 3,000 shareholders over a range of controversial issues. Solomon Lew, the largest shareholder in Coles Myer, and his fellow director, former New South Wales Premier Nick Greiner, were re-elected to the board despite a massive protest vote. Page 1.

Amid mounting concerns that Australia's commitment to trade liberalisation is waning, the Federal Government has signalled a dramatic change in trade policy, indicating that Australia will cut its tariffs only if other APEC countries do the same. The change is outlined in the Government's proposals for Australia at this weekend's APEC summit in the Philippines. Page 1.

Although merchandise imports rose one percent in October to A$6.32 billion in seasonally adjusted terms, market economists have questioned the Budget's upbeat business investment forecasts for the current financial year following the fall of

imports of cpital goods to A$1.4 billion. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, overall imports are still trending lower and monthly import bills remain well short of the levels they reached in the first half of calendar 1996. Page 3.

The Northern Territory Government will today announce a Phillips Petroleum Co plan to develop a A$1.9 billion onshore liquefied natural gas project, based in Darwin, which will receive gas from the Bayou-Undan discovery in the Timor Gap via a 470 km sub-sea pipeline. It will be the first development of a hydrocarbon discovery in the so-called Zone of Cooperation.
Page 19.

While he said the outcome of the next six weeks was difficult to predict, David Jones Ltd chairman Dick Warburton told yesterday's annual general meeting that the upmarket retailer could expect lower pre-tax profits this financial year unless there was an improvement in sales in the crucial Christmas period and throughout the rest of the year. Page 19.

Qantas Airways Ltd has indirectly invested in the rival alliance formed by Air New Zealand Ltd and Ansett Holdings Ltd by taking up its NZ$47 million share of Air NZ's NZ$242 million rights issue. Air NZ said yesterday that its pro rata issue of 121 millon new shares to shareholders had been 98 percent subscribed and Qantas is believed to have exercised it full entitlement to maintain its strategic shareholding at 19.4 percent. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Coles Myer unity ticket was rocked yesterday when the Myer family, which controls eight percent of the group, voted against the re-election of director Nick Greiner at a marathon six-and-a-half hour annual meeting. Although comfortably re-elected, Greiner's appointment saw the largest protest vote registered against any of the seven successful candidates. Page 41.

Canadian mining house Corriente Resources Inc said results provided by BHP Minerals for the first three drill holes at the Taca-Taca copper-gold deposit in Argentina, in which Corriente is a partner, indicated results equal to those at BHP's spectacular Chilean copper project, Escondida. Page 41.

In a deal which is the latest in a battle for consumer loyalty which is changing the face of the credit card market, Volvo and the Commonwealth Bank have unveiled the Volvo Gold Card deal, under which new and used registered Volvo drivers who use the card will pick up as many as 20 bonus
points, which go towards a free trip, for every dollar spent at affiliated businesses. Page 41.

As Coca-Cola Amatil shares plunged 40 cents yesterday to close at A$15.10 because of readjusted profit valuations, managing director Norb Cole defended the company's decision to wait until last Friday to warn the market that profits for this year would be flat. Page 43.

Following an announcement by Malaysian State-owned petroleum giant Petronas that it was looking to succeed BHP as operator of the Dai Hung oil field, BHP has confirmed it is holding discussions with its four partners in the project which could result in Petronas assuming control of the troubled Vietnamese project. Page 43.

Following an extensive search through a strong field of international and domestic contenders, the Federal Government has appointed Stephen Grenville, who has been the Reserve Bank's assistant economic governor since 1992 and a senior bank
official since 1982, as the bank's deputy governor. Page 43.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

A marathon six-and-a-half hour meeting yesterday saw the re-election of Solomon Lew and six other members of Coles Myer's "unity slate" of directors. However there were reports late yesterday that the Myer family had voted its 8.5 percent, 92 million shae block against Nick Greiner as a protest against Greiner's opposition to the family's participation in the board shuffle that occurred in the wake of the Yannon affair last year. Page 31.

Making his debut as a Coles Myer director yesterday, Brierley Investments boss Paul Collins, along with the other board members, faced a barrage of lectures and complaints as 1,500 shareholders tackled Coles about what was undoubtedly the worst year in th giant retailer's history. Page 31.

The Energy Star program - a US initiative aiming to reduce the power consumption of office electrical equipment such as computers and faxes - which is currently being introduced into Australia by New South Wales' Sustainable Energy Development
Authority is an effort to cut greenhouse gas emissions and save business money, has been praised by United States President Bill Clinton. Page 31.

Following the release of an Australian Bureau of Statistics report showing capital imports had dropped eight percent, seasonally adjusted, in October to A$1.4 billion, Opposition Treasurer Gareth Evans quoted Bankers Trust chief economist Chris Catons report on the figures, which said the ABS report constitutes another sign of a soft economy, to defend his comments to Federal Treasurer Peter Costello that the economy
was flat. Page 31.

Speaking at the first annual meeting as a listed company, David Jones chairman Dick Warburton told the retailer's 600 investors the next 36 days to Christmas will be crucial for the group, particularly in determining whether profits and dividends will be cut this financial year. Page 33.

Defending the timing of Coca-Cola Amatil's Friday announcement that its 1996 profit would be flat in the face of market concerns that the beverage giant had waited too long, managing director Norb Cole said Amatil had decided it was time to make the annoucement after its trading results for October became available. Page 33.
THE AGE

Although Solomon Lew and six other members of Coles Myer's "unity slate" of directors were re-elected at a meeting yesterday, it is believed one major shareholder used its shares to try and block the re-election of Nick Greiner. Arnold Hancock, head of the Myer family company, Barclay Investments, said after the meeting that the Myer family supported the present board and its members, but he refused to comment on which way the family had voted on Greiner's nomination. Page C1.

With its diamond hopes, some cash and an exploration focus on the Yilgarn block of Western Australia, Joseph Gutnick's Astro Mining NL yesterday surpassed Ashton Mining in total market value after shares rose to A$7.82, valuing the company at A$559 million. Page C1.

David Jones Ltd chairman Dick Warburton told shareholders yesterday that the next 36 days would be crucial for the upmarket retailer and if profits failed to grow there would probably be a cut in dividends. However, he said he was encouraged by the recen Westpac/Melbourne Institute consumer
survey which showed a marginal upsurge in demand. Page C1.

After giving an address to the Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce yesterday, Coca-Cola Amatil managing director Norb Cole defended his company's decision to announce a flat profit for 1996 on Friday, claiming CCA was waiting for its lower-than-expected trading results for October to become available before making an announcement. Page C3.

In its monthly production figures released yesterday, BHP said production of its raw steel in the five months to date had totalled 3.54 million tonnes, down from 3.64 million tonnes in the same period last year because of lower production at its Newcastle steelworks following a reline of one of its blast furnaces at the site. Page C3.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello announced yesterday former diplomat and Indonesia specialist Dr Stephen Grenville would take up the position of deputy governor of the Reserve Bank. Grenville has been with the bank for 14 years as an economic
adviser and since 1992 as the assistant governor for the economy. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
